verdict.rationale: Lithic's own Auth Rules engine lets users configure rules that run automatically in the background. Without further intervention, the rules make decisions on every authorization, 3DS, tokenization and ACH event, with no extra infrastructure, and the agentic-commerce page claims 'autonomous' controls. This is narrow, event-triggered rule automation rather than general-purpose background automations; MCP/API execution happens in-editor on demand, not autonomously. Missing for 10: general workflow/automation builder, scheduled or recurring background jobs, autonomous agent-driven actions beyond authorization decisioning, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: you can enforce business-specific authorization logic at the program, account, or card level, without managing additional infrastructure

the Auth Rules engine supports multiple event streams, each enabling decisioning for a different payment flow: card authorizations, 3DS authentication, digital wallet and merchant tokenization, and ACH receipts.
secure and autonomous issuing, payments, and controls for AI-powered workflows
